name: Calendula
grown_as: Pot marigold, a hardy annual sown each spring and often self-seeding. William's library lists 'Art Shades', a mix of soft apricot, peach, orange, cream and gold flowers, mostly double or semi-double. Drawn here in orange, the commonest shade. ⚠️ CHECK the colour William would like drawn.
habit: A bushy, branched annual 30 to 60 cm high and about 30 cm across, upright to sprawling. The whole plant is softly hairy, slightly sticky and smells resinous when touched.

leaf.outline: Lower leaves spoon-shaped (widest near the tip), 5 to 15 cm; upper leaves narrower, oblong to lance-shaped
leaf.base: Lower leaves narrow into a winged stalk; upper leaves stalkless, half-clasping the stem
leaf.margin: Smooth or with a few small, widely spaced teeth, often slightly wavy
leaf.veins: A clear pale midrib; side veins faint
leaf.surface: Soft and slightly sticky with short glandular hairs on both sides; a little fleshy
leaf.stalk: None, or a short winged stalk on the lowest leaves

flower.form: A flat open daisy head; in 'Art Shades' mostly double or semi-double, with several rows of rays
flower.petals: Many strap-shaped ray florets, the tip cut square with two or three tiny teeth
flower.colour: Orange (the mix also gives apricot, peach, cream and gold)
flower.centre: A disc of small tubular florets, orange, yellow or dark brown; smaller and partly hidden in double flowers
flower.behind: One or two rows of narrow, pointed, equal green bracts, sticky-hairy
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of the branches on stout stalks that thicken under the head, facing up. Closes at night and in dull weather

fruit: A ring of dry, strongly curved seeds where the flower was: the outer ones C-shaped or boat-shaped, knobbly and ridged on the back, the inner ones curled almost into rings. Beige to brown when ripe.
seedling: Two oblong, thick, smooth seed leaves with rounded tips. The first true leaves are spoon-shaped, soft and slightly hairy.
winter: An annual. In a mild winter some plants survive and flower on; self-sown seedlings may sit through winter as small rosettes.

leaf: simple spoon-shaped to oblong leaf, widest towards the rounded tip
edge smooth or with a few small far-spaced teeth
no proper stalk: the base narrows or clasps the stem
bloom: many strap-shaped orange rays with square, finely notched tips
several rows of rays (double or semi-double)
young: alternate spoon-shaped leaves clasping the stem
flower: many flat orange heads, one at each branch tip, held just above the leaves
seedhead: a ring of curled, hooked brown seeds where the flower was

look_alikes: French and African marigolds (Tagetes) have finely cut leaves, a strong pungent smell, a smooth tube of bracts and straight thin seeds. Field marigold (Calendula arvensis) has heads only 1 to 2 cm across. Corn marigold has lobed blue-green leaves and yellow heads.
